scope: Making foundation models (LLMs and VLMs) faithfully adhere to specified principles: honesty, appropriate refusal and corrigibility that hold under pressure, and telling genuine adherence from surface compliance in preference-based alignment.
scope_include: value alignment and specification adherence: training or checking models to follow written principles, constitutions or model specs
honesty: lying, deception, sycophancy, hallucination presented as fact, calibration and admitting uncertainty
harmlessness and refusal: refusing harmful requests, over-refusal of benign ones, refusal behavior and its mechanisms
robustness of safety behavior under pressure: jailbreaks, prompt injection, misleading context, fine-tuning attacks, when they explain why principles fail
corrigibility and controllability: following legitimate instructions, accepting correction or shutdown, instruction hierarchy
alignment faking, deceptive alignment, scheming, reward hacking and specification gaming
how preference-based alignment (RLHF, DPO, reward models, preference data) shapes the above, including theory
scope_exclude: models that are not LLMs or VLMs
alignment or post-training only for task performance (math, code, agents) with no safety, honesty or control angle
new attack recipes with no analysis of why the model's principles fail
applications or benchmarks in a single domain with no general method or finding

summary.language: Korean, keeping technical terms in English
